text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers.
- Austria follows the international move and raises petrol prices by 0.2 schillings in the wake of the Iraqi crisis.
- Creditanstalt employees are against Die Erste savings bank taking the helm in the event of the privatisation of Austria's number two bank.
- Electric Industry Union wants electricity prices for private users to be raised as prices for industrial users fall due to the liberalisation of the market by the EU.
- Die Erste will likely not take the majority stake in the holding company it has proposed forming with Creditanstalt due to opposition from Germany's Commerzbank.
- Study shows Austria's computer market is lagging. Only a quarter of Austrian homes has a personal computer, compared to about 40 percent in the Netherlands, Europe's leader.
- Short-time work has risen steeply within the last year to 8,505 employees in July from 3,667 the year before, mainly in the metal and paper industries.
- VA Tech will merge its electrotechnical branches Elin Energieanwendung and Elektrobau.
